related_resources.reason: Fourier coefficients, orthogonality, period and harmonic decomposition.
Parity, shifting, convergence, Gibbs phenomenon and Fourier operations.

authorship.scope: Original foundation-first Fourier and periodic-forcing lecture with non-spoken mathematical companion; earlier manuscripts retained.

prerequisites.reason: Compute Fourier coefficients and understand what a partial harmonic sum means.

recommended.reason: Optional review of sinusoidal motion, period, amplitude and phase.

background: Elementary calculus, sine and cosine, first-order initial-value problems, and basic forced oscillators; no functional analysis or PDE background.
readiness_checks: Use orthogonality to derive best mean-square approximation.
Calculate the first harmonic energy of a square wave.
Explain why mean-square convergence and a visible Gibbs overshoot can coexist.

description: Explains Fourier series as orthogonal projection, develops convergence and energy identities, and analyzes the Gibbs phenomenon for discontinuous signals.
